newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: HSBC Argentine purchase not a surprise - analysts.
newsitem.headline: HSBC Argentine purchase not a surprise - analysts.

text.p: The purchase of Argentine private financial services holding Grupo Roberts announced Friday by HSBC Holdings Plc was no surprise after two major Spanish banks took control this month of two top Argentine banks, analysts said.
"This is the natural transition from being a minor stakeholder to being a major one," said an analyst for Merchant Bankers, an affiliate of Salomon Brothers.
Pedro Rabassa, economist for local Banco Quilmes, said "there is no reason to think the process of mergers and acquisitions in Argentina has come to a halt."

"There is huge investment interest from foreign banks. There is annual growth of about 20 percent in Argentina's monetary base and most analysts expect it to hold around those levels in coming years."
Ignacio Lafuente, head trader for Banco Frances, said the HSBC deal would make the banking sector more solid although he warned against excessive concentration.
"Banking concentration will be very positive for the public with the possible launching of new services but it also entails the risk of overconcentration," Lafuente said.
When the Mexican devaluation crisis struck in December 1994, Argentina had 168 public or private banks. By last October, they had shrunk to 118 through closures or mergers.

Spain's Santander announced this week it bought a 35.06 percent stake in local Banco Rio for $594 million with an option to buy another 15 percent. The first stake involves voting control. Earlier this month, fellow Spanish bank Bilbao bought 71.8 percent of Banco Frances for $466 million.
"The decision was helped by recent purchases in Argentina by Spain's Banco Santander and Banco de Bilbao Vizcaya."

HSBC said in a statement in London the bank would buy all the shares issued in Grupo Roberts, a holding that includes Banco Roberts, for between $600 and $688 million. HSBC already had an indirect stake of 29.9 percent in Banco Roberts.

"The announcement by HSBC was no surprise as the Argentine market offers great opportunities due its low banking penetration and good economic prospects," the commercial manager for a major foreign bank said.
Vivi Munoz, analyst for Credit Lyonnais, said the expected growth of the Argentine banking sector "is amazing."

Banking penetration in Argentina was 19 percent in 1995 against 24 percent in Brazil, 33 percent in Mexico, 40 percent in Chile and 95 percent in Spain, she said. Penetration is expected to grow in Argentina to 24 percent this year and 25 percent next year.
"This is the time for major banks to take positions in Argentina," she said.
Grupo Roberts has also interests in the insurance, health care and pension fund sectors as well as a stake of about 12 percent in footwear and textile firm Alpargatas SA.
It will hold a news conference in Buenos Aires at 1300 local (1600 GMT) to offer details of the purchase by HSBC, which also has interests in Mexico, Brazil, Chile and peru.
